messages:
customer-support: FYI — acme-inc reporting a spike of 504s and timeouts to hosted inference since 09:22 UTC. Lots of long-sequence requests.
jamal: ok digging in. Any trace ids or example request ids?
maria: trace IDs: trace-9a2f, trace-9a3b. p95 jumped from ~180ms to ~2.3s. Errors are Gateway/504.
devon: saw alerts from queue-depth: continuous-batcher backlog > 95% and dequeue latency spiking. Looks like kvcache warmup + big sequences.
opsbot: Alert: hosted.gateway.request_latency.p95 > 1500ms for tenant acme-inc (rule triggered).
jamal: repro curl from support (sanitized):
```bash
curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/hosted/generate" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ***" \ 
  -d '{"model":"longform-1","input":"<~12k tokens>...","max_tokens":1024}'
# response: HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout\n```
maria: logs show enqueue times stacking up. continuous-batcher queue depth reached configured limit and started early-rejecting some requests, others stuck waiting and hit client timeout.
alex: stack traces reference batcher:batch_loop -> dequeue() hang near kvcache.populate() when eviction thrash happens.
devon: quick mitigation options: 1) bump batcher concurrency on affected pool, 2) increase queue depth threshold for short window, 3) temporarily route acme-inc traffic to backup region/model variant.
jamal: can we try bumping pool size by +2 and throttle large sequences? I'll open a canary route to redirect 20% of traffic to fallback model.
customer-support: customer is asking for ETA and if there’s a quick fix. They can accept degraded throughput if latency improves.
maria: doing a small change: increasing batcher worker_count from 12 -> 16 for pool hosted-prod-1. Applying now.
opsbot: Deploy triggered by maria: infra/change/6632100456-batcher-scale (rollout started).
(devon): I’m also enabling short-sequence prioritization (prefetch priority rule) for 10m to reduce head-of-line blocking.
alex: monitor points — queue_depth, dequeue_latency, batch_size_distribution, kvcache_miss_rate. If kvcache miss rate spikes, we may need kvcache prewarm or slower eviction.
jamal: post-change metrics: queue_depth dropped 60% in 90s, p95 down from 2300ms -> 420ms. A few 504s remain while inflight backlog drains.
maria: leaving throttles: early-reject threshold set to 95th -> 99th for 5m window to avoid cascade.
customer-support: customer confirmed degraded-but-working, fewer 504s now. Thanks.
sre-bot: Note: follow-up runbook item created to add longer kvcache warmup for longseq workloads and to run load test for 12k token traces. ID: RB-3281.
jamal: root cause summary: sudden increase of long-sequence requests caused continuous-batcher queue to saturate; kvcache warmup and eviction thrash increased dequeue times; hitting queue depth limits produced a mix of early-rejects and tail timeouts (504). Mitigations: scale batcher, prioritize short sequences, temporary routing to fallback model, and adjust kvcache warmup.
alex: follow-ups: create automated autoscale trigger for sustained queue_depth > 70% for >2m, and add tenant-level longseq throttling opt-in.
customer-support: closing loop with acme-inc, asked them to stagger long requests where possible. They will report if any further regressions. :thumbsup:
